title: Generating Function of Positive Compositions: ∑ₙ #(positive comps) Xⁿ = Xᵏ/(1−X)ᵏ
description: A positive (strong) composition of n into k parts is a function g : Fin k → ℕ with every part ≥ 1 and ∑ᵢ g(i) = n. The parent generating-function entry (oq-01) shows the ordinary generating function of the WEAK-composition counts is W k = invOneSubPow S k = 1/(1−X)ᵏ; the sibling oq-03 counts positive compositions as C(n−1, k−1) via an explicit ±1 bijection with weak compositions of n−k. This entry packages the positive-composition counts as a generating function P k = ∑ₙ #{g : Fin k → ℕ // (∀ i, 1 ≤ g i) ∧ ∑ i, g i = n} · Xⁿ ∈ S⟦X⟧ over any commutative ring S, and proves the factored identity P k = Xᵏ · W k = Xᵏ/(1−X)ᵏ (positiveCompositionGenFun_eq), holding for EVERY k with no positivity hypothesis. The Xᵏ factor is the algebraic shadow of the ±1 bijection 'subtract 1 from each of the k parts', which lowers the degree by exactly k. The proof is coefficientwise: Mathlib's coeff_X_pow_mul' gives coeff n (Xᵏ · W k) = ite (k ≤ n) (coeff (n−k) (W k)) 0; for k ≤ n the sibling's positiveCompositionEquivWeak bijects positive compositions of n with weak compositions of n−k (so the counts agree), and for n < k there is no positive composition of n into k positive parts (the subtype is empty). The Xᵏ/(1−X)ᵏ form (positiveCompositionGenFun_eq_X_pow_mul_invOneSubPow) and the relation P k · (1−X)ᵏ = Xᵏ (positiveCompositionGenFun_mul_one_sub_pow) then follow from the parent's weak-composition identities (0 < k), and the coefficient reads off as C(n−1, k−1) for 0 < k ≤ n (coeff_positiveCompositionGenFun_eq_choose). The new content beyond Mathlib and the two imported siblings is the identification of the enumerative generating function of POSITIVE-composition counts with the shifted algebraic series Xᵏ · invOneSubPow.

This entry uses positiveCompositionEquivWeak coefficientwise to match counts for k ≤ n, the emptiness of the subtype for n < k, and card_positiveComposition for the closed-form coefficient corollary.

Sibling refinement in the same family. OQ-02 bounds every part above (≤ b) and obtains the inclusion–exclusion generating function ((1−x^{b+1})/(1−x))ᵏ. This entry bounds every part below (≥ 1), multiplying the shared 1/(1−x)ᵏ denominator by xᵏ instead. Together with the parent (unrestricted) they trace how lower/upper part-constraints deform the numerator while preserving the 1/(1−x)ᵏ core.

meta.assumptions: 0 axioms, 0 sorries, no native_decide. All public results — positiveCompositionGenFun_eq (P k = Xᵏ · W k, every k), positiveCompositionGenFun_eq_X_pow_mul_invOneSubPow (P k = Xᵏ · invOneSubPow S k, 0 < k), positiveCompositionGenFun_mul_one_sub_pow (P k · (1−X)ᵏ = Xᵏ, 0 < k), coeff_positiveCompositionGenFun_eq_choose (coefficient is C(n−1, k−1) for 0 < k ≤ n), and the convolution layer weakCompositionGenFun_mul / positiveCompositionGenFun_mul (P j · P k = P (j+k), 0 < j, 0 < k) / card_positiveComposition_convolution (the coefficient-level Vandermonde ∑_{a+b=n} #pos(a,j)·#pos(b,k) = #pos(n,j+k)) — were verified with #print axioms to depend only on the foundational propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound. The factored identity P k = Xᵏ · W k holds for ALL k (the k = 0 case gives P 0 = W 0); the invOneSubPow and (1−X)ᵏ corollaries inherit the parent's 0 < k hypothesis (which feeds the weak series' inverse relation). The new content beyond Mathlib is the identification of the enumerative generating function of positive-composition counts with the shifted algebraic series Xᵏ · invOneSubPow; Mathlib supplies the multiplication-by-Xᵏ coefficient rule coeff_X_pow_mul', the parent supplies the weak generating function, and the sibling oq-03 supplies the ±1 bijection positiveCompositionEquivWeak and the count card_positiveComposition. Sanity check: at k = 1 the series is ∑_{n≥1} 1·Xⁿ = X/(1−X) (every n ≥ 1 has the unique positive composition (n), and n = 0 has none); at k = 2 the coefficient of Xⁿ is n−1 = C(n−1, 1) for n ≥ 2, the n−1 positive compositions (i, n−i) with 1 ≤ i ≤ n−1.

overview.historicalContext: A composition of n is an ordered tuple of positive integers summing to n; fixing the number of parts k, the number of compositions of n into exactly k positive parts is the classical C(n−1, k−1) (place k−1 of the n−1 internal bars). Its generating function is the negative-binomial series shifted by the degree of its smallest term: ∑ₙ C(n−1, k−1) xⁿ = (x/(1−x))ᵏ = xᵏ/(1−x)ᵏ. The xᵏ records that every part is at least 1, so the smallest composition counted has total k; dividing out xᵏ recovers the unrestricted 1/(1−x)ᵏ of weak compositions. This is the lower-bound counterpart of the bounded-parts (upper-bound) deformation, and the two together express how part-constraints reshape the numerator of the rational generating function while the 1/(1−x)ᵏ denominator — one geometric factor per part — persists. Algebraically the shift is the substitution xᵢ ↦ 1 + xᵢ in each geometric series factor, the generating-function avatar of the ±1 bijection between strong and weak compositions.
overview.problemStatement: Show that the ordinary generating function of the positive-composition counts, P(x) = ∑ₙ #{g : Fin k → ℕ | (∀ i, g(i) ≥ 1) ∧ ∑ᵢ g(i) = n} xⁿ, is xᵏ/(1−x)ᵏ; equivalently, that P(x) = xᵏ · W(x) where W is the weak-composition generating function 1/(1−x)ᵏ, recovering the n-th coefficient as C(n−1, k−1) for 0 < k ≤ n.
overview.text: The parent entry (oq-01) forms the weak-composition generating function W k = mk (n ↦ #weak comps) over an arbitrary commutative ring S and identifies it with Mathlib's invOneSubPow S k = 1/(1−X)ᵏ. The sibling oq-03 supplies the positive-composition Fintype instance and the explicit ±1 bijection positiveCompositionEquivWeak: for k ≤ n, positive compositions of n into k parts biject with weak compositions of n−k. This entry forms the positive-composition generating function P k = mk (n ↦ #positive comps) in S⟦X⟧ and proves P k = Xᵏ · W k coefficientwise, then specializes to the Xᵏ/(1−X)ᵏ and Xᵏ-residue forms.
overview.proofStrategy: Define positiveCompositionGenFun S k = PowerSeries.mk (fun n => (Fintype.card {g : Fin k → ℕ // (∀ i, 1 ≤ g i) ∧ ∑ i, g i = n} : S)); coeff_positiveCompositionGenFun reads its coefficients as casts of the counts. The headline positiveCompositionGenFun_eq proves P k = Xᵏ · W k for every k by PowerSeries.ext: Mathlib's coeff_X_pow_mul' rewrites the right-hand coefficient as ite (k ≤ n) (coeff (n−k) (W k)) 0. In the k ≤ n branch, coeff_weakCompositionGenFun turns coeff (n−k) (W k) into the cast of #weak comps of n−k, and Fintype.card_congr applied to the sibling's positiveCompositionEquivWeak k n equates that with #positive comps of n. In the n < k branch, an IsEmpty instance (no function Fin k → ℕ with all parts ≥ 1 can sum to less than k) makes the positive count 0, matching the else-branch via Fintype.card_eq_zero. The corollary positiveCompositionGenFun_eq_X_pow_mul_invOneSubPow rewrites W k by the parent's weakCompositionGenFun_eq_invOneSubPow (0 < k) to land at Xᵏ · invOneSubPow S k. positiveCompositionGenFun_mul_one_sub_pow multiplies through and applies the parent's weakCompositionGenFun_mul_one_sub_pow (W k · (1−X)ᵏ = 1) to conclude P k · (1−X)ᵏ = Xᵏ. coeff_positiveCompositionGenFun_eq_choose rewrites the coefficient by the sibling's card_positiveComposition to give C(n−1, k−1) for 0 < k ≤ n.
keyInsights: **The Xᵏ factor IS the ±1 bijection**: subtracting 1 from each of the k parts of a positive composition of n produces a weak composition of n−k, and at the generating-function level this degree-lowering bijection is exactly multiplication by Xᵏ. The combinatorial bijection (sibling oq-03) and the algebraic shift (this entry) are two faces of the same fact, joined by coeff_X_pow_mul'.

**The factored identity needs no positivity hypothesis**: positiveCompositionGenFun_eq holds for every k, including k = 0, because its proof only uses the bijection (for k ≤ n) and emptiness (for n < k) — both unconditional. The 0 < k hypothesis enters only when passing to invOneSubPow and (1−X)ᵏ, where it is inherited from the parent's weak-series identities. This cleanly separates the purely combinatorial content from the algebraic packaging.

**Emptiness handles the boundary cleanly**: for n < k there is no positive composition (k positive parts force a total ≥ k > n), so the count is 0 — exactly the else-branch of coeff_X_pow_mul'. Proving the subtype IsEmpty (a part-sum lower bound by Finset.sum_le_sum) avoids any case juggling and makes both sides vanish identically; the closed form C(n−1, k−1) is therefore stated only for k ≤ n, where ℕ truncation does not distort it.

**Reuse over reproof**: every nontrivial ingredient is imported — the weak series and its inverse relation from the parent, the ±1 bijection and the closed count from the sibling, the multiplication-by-Xᵏ rule from Mathlib. The entry's own work is the bridge identifying the positive generating function with Xᵏ · W k; it adds a new theorem family without re-deriving any combinatorics already in the gallery.

**Works over any commutative ring**: like the parent, both the generating function and the identity are stated over an arbitrary commutative ring S with counts cast through ℕ → S, so the result is purely formal — independent of characteristic or convergence, matching the generality of invOneSubPow.

**Concatenation is multiplication of series**: the positive-composition generating functions form a multiplicative semigroup indexed by part-count, P j · P k = P (j+k) (positiveCompositionGenFun_mul). This is the exact algebraic shadow of concatenating compositions — gluing a positive composition into j parts onto one into k parts is a bijection onto compositions into j+k parts — and it is precisely the Xᵏ-shift of Mathlib's invOneSubPow_add semigroup law. Reading off the Cauchy-product coefficient (card_positiveComposition_convolution) recovers the upper-index Vandermonde convolution ∑_{a+b=n} C(a−1,j−1)·C(b−1,k−1) = C(n−1,j+k−1) in count form, with the vanishing of the count off j ≤ a ≤ n−k sidestepping the truncated-ℕ pitfalls that plague the raw binomial statement.
prerequisites: The weak-composition generating function W k and its identification with invOneSubPow S k from the parent entry (Proofs/StarsAndBarsWeakCompositionsOQ01.lean): weakCompositionGenFun, coeff_weakCompositionGenFun, weakCompositionGenFun_eq_invOneSubPow, weakCompositionGenFun_mul_one_sub_pow

The positive-composition Fintype instance and the explicit ±1 bijection positiveCompositionEquivWeak, plus the closed count card_positiveComposition (C(n−1, k−1)), from the sibling entry (Proofs/StarsAndBarsWeakCompositionsOQ03.lean)
Formal power series over a commutative ring: PowerSeries.mk, coeff, coeff_mk, extensionality PowerSeries.ext, and the multiplication-by-Xᵏ coefficient rule PowerSeries.coeff_X_pow_mul'
Fintype.card_congr (transport a cardinality across an equiv) and Fintype.card_eq_zero (a cardinality is 0 for an empty type)
Finset.sum_le_sum / Finset.sum_const to bound a sum of k parts each ≥ 1 below by k, giving the emptiness of positive compositions of n < k

sections.title: The Generating Function of Positive-Composition Counts
sections.mathContext: $P_k(X) = \sum_{n} \#\{g : \mathrm{Fin}\,k \to \mathbb{N} \mid (\forall i,\, g(i) \ge 1) \wedge \textstyle\sum_i g(i) = n\}\, X^n \in S\llbracket X\rrbracket$.
sections.summary: The module docstring fixes the object (the ordinary generating function of the positive/strong-composition counts over an arbitrary commutative ring S) and the target Xᵏ/(1−X)ᵏ. positiveCompositionGenFun packages the counts as mk (n ↦ (card {g : Fin k → ℕ // (∀ i, 1 ≤ g i) ∧ ∑ g = n} : S)), with the Fintype instance imported from the sibling oq-03, and the simp lemma coeff_positiveCompositionGenFun reads its n-th coefficient straight off as the cast of the count. It records the gap: the weak generating function (parent) and the positive count/bijection (sibling) exist, but their generating-function bridge — that the positive series is the Xᵏ-shift of the weak one — is new.

sections.title: The Factored Identity P k = Xᵏ · W k (every k)
sections.summary: positiveCompositionGenFun_eq is the headline and holds for every k. By PowerSeries.ext and Mathlib's coeff_X_pow_mul', the n-th coefficient of Xᵏ · W k is coeff (n−k) (W k) when k ≤ n and 0 otherwise. In the k ≤ n branch, coeff_weakCompositionGenFun and Fintype.card_congr (positiveCompositionEquivWeak k n) identify #positive comps of n with #weak comps of n−k. In the n < k branch, an IsEmpty proof (k positive parts sum to ≥ k > n, via Finset.sum_le_sum) makes the positive count 0 (Fintype.card_eq_zero), matching the else-branch. No positivity hypothesis is needed.

sections.title: Xᵏ/(1−X)ᵏ and the Residue Relation
sections.summary: positiveCompositionGenFun_eq_X_pow_mul_invOneSubPow rewrites the weak series by the parent's weakCompositionGenFun_eq_invOneSubPow (0 < k) to present P k as Xᵏ · invOneSubPow S k = Xᵏ/(1−X)ᵏ. positiveCompositionGenFun_mul_one_sub_pow multiplies P k by (1−X)ᵏ, reassociates, and applies the parent's weakCompositionGenFun_mul_one_sub_pow (W k · (1−X)ᵏ = 1) to conclude P k · (1−X)ᵏ = Xᵏ — the formal statement that P k is Xᵏ times the inverse of (1−X)ᵏ.

sections.title: Reading Off the Coefficients
sections.mathContext: $[X^n]\, X^k/(1-X)^k = \#\{g \mid g \ge 1,\ \textstyle\sum g = n\} = \binom{n-1}{k-1}\ (0 < k \le n)$.
sections.summary: coeff_positiveCompositionGenFun_eq_card restates the coefficient as the positive-composition count, and coeff_positiveCompositionGenFun_eq_choose specializes it to the closed form C(n−1, k−1) for 0 < k ≤ n by rewriting through the sibling's card_positiveComposition. These are the term-by-term face of the generating-function identity — the classical statement that the compositions-into-k-positive-parts numbers are the coefficients of xᵏ/(1−x)ᵏ.

sections.title: Convolution: Concatenation of Compositions
sections.summary: The factored forms turn Mathlib's semigroup law invOneSubPow_add (invOneSubPow S (j+k) = invOneSubPow S j · invOneSubPow S k) into multiplicative laws on the generating functions. weakCompositionGenFun_mul proves W j · W k = W (j+k) for 0 < j, k by rewriting each factor to (invOneSubPow S ·).val and applying invOneSubPow_add with Units.val_mul. positiveCompositionGenFun_mul is the headline: P j · P k = P (j+k), the Xᵏ-shift of the weak law (P j · P k = Xʲ⁺ᵏ · W j · W k = Xʲ⁺ᵏ · W (j+k) = P (j+k)), the generating-function avatar of concatenating a positive composition into j parts with one into k parts. Reading off the Xⁿ coefficient via the Cauchy product (PowerSeries.coeff_mul) gives card_positiveComposition_convolution, the upper-index (negative-binomial) Vandermonde convolution ∑_{a+b=n} #pos(a,j)·#pos(b,k) = #pos(n,j+k) stated at the count level — the positive counts vanish off j ≤ a ≤ n−k, so no truncated-subtraction conventions intrude.

conclusion.summary: The generating-function form of positive (strong) compositions is formalized sorry-free and axiom-free: the ordinary generating function P k = ∑ₙ #(positive compositions of n into k parts) Xⁿ over any commutative ring equals Xᵏ times the weak-composition generating function (positiveCompositionGenFun_eq, every k), hence Xᵏ · invOneSubPow S k = Xᵏ/(1−X)ᵏ for 0 < k (positiveCompositionGenFun_eq_X_pow_mul_invOneSubPow), so P k · (1−X)ᵏ = Xᵏ (positiveCompositionGenFun_mul_one_sub_pow) and the n-th coefficient is C(n−1, k−1) for 0 < k ≤ n (coeff_positiveCompositionGenFun_eq_choose). The convolution layer adds the semigroup law: W j · W k = W (j+k) (weakCompositionGenFun_mul) and its Xᵏ-shift P j · P k = P (j+k) (positiveCompositionGenFun_mul) for 0 < j, k — the generating-function form of concatenating compositions — whose Cauchy-product coefficient is the upper-index Vandermonde convolution ∑_{a+b=n} #pos(a,j)·#pos(b,k) = #pos(n,j+k) (card_positiveComposition_convolution). The content beyond Mathlib and the imported siblings is the identification of the enumerative generating function of positive-composition counts with the shifted algebraic series Xᵏ · invOneSubPow, together with the concatenation semigroup structure, mediated coefficientwise by the ±1 bijection (k ≤ n) and emptiness (n < k).
conclusion.implications: The Xᵏ-shift makes precise, at the level of equal power series, that strong and weak compositions differ only by the degree-k displacement of subtracting 1 from each part: every algebraic fact about invOneSubPow transfers to positive compositions after this shift. Placed beside the parent (unrestricted, 1/(1−x)ᵏ) and the bounded-parts sibling (((1−x^{b+1})/(1−x))ᵏ), it completes the lower/upper/none trichotomy of part-constraints over the shared 1/(1−x)ᵏ denominator, and is the natural base case for a general 'generating function of constrained compositions' development.
openQuestions: Unify the weak, positive, and bounded-parts generating functions into a single parameterized identity: for parts constrained to an interval [a, b], the generating function is ((xᵃ − x^{b+1})/(1−x))ᵏ, specializing to xᵏ/(1−x)ᵏ (a = 1, b = ∞), 1/(1−x)ᵏ (a = 0, b = ∞), and the bounded sibling. Formalize this as one theorem with the three current entries as corollaries.

Derive the positive-composition total ∑ₖ P k = x/(1−2x) (compositions of n into any number of positive parts, count 2^{n−1}) by summing the geometric series ∑ₖ (x/(1−x))ᵏ in S⟦X⟧, connecting this entry to the classical 2^{n−1} composition count.
